angle: The ruthless strategy and cold-blooded pragmatism of the man who built an empire.
hook: Chanakya once turned 1 gold coin into 8 using a secret technique.
points: He was thrown out of the royal court for being ugly and having crooked feet.
He trained Chandragupta for 7 years after testing his loyalty by killing a rival.
He realized his mistake in attacking the capital first after hearing a mother scold her son.
He secretly poisoned the emperor's food daily to build immunity against assassination attempts.
True power requires removing emotion and prioritizing the long-term objective above all else.
closer: Are you building your empire or just playing at it?

evidence.hook: He made 800 million gold coins (kahapanas), using a secret technique that allowed him to turn 1 coin into 8 coins.
points: Disgusted by his appearance, the emperor ordered him to be thrown out of the assembly.
Chandragupta retrieved the woolen thread by cutting off Pabbata's head. For the next seven years, Chanakya trained Chandragupta for imperial duties.
The woman scolded him, saying that he was eating food like Chandragupta, who attacked the central part of the empire instead of conquering the border villages first.
Chanakya started mixing small doses of poison in the new emperor's food to make him immune to poisoning attempts by the enemies.
Chanakya then bound his top knot, having achieved his objective, and retired.

caption: Chanakya understood that sentimentality is a weakness that destroys leaders. He manipulated, schemed, and operated in the shadows to secure a legacy that lasted generations. What are you willing to sacrifice to ensure your vision becomes reality?
